newsitem.title: GERMANY: Hoechst sees better Q2, higher 97 profit.
newsitem.headline: Hoechst sees better Q2, higher 97 profit.

text.p: German chemicals and drugs group Hoechst AG said on Monday that it expects its second quarter to be distinctly improved as compared with the first quarter.
"Our expectation is that the second quarter will be much better than the first quarter," Hoechst chief financial officer Klaus-Juergen Schmieder told Reuters in a telephone interview.
He said this prediction referred mainly to profits.
Schmieder also said that on a comparable basis the group expects its 1997 operating profit will be much higher than last year's operating profit.
"On a comparable basis, we expect a clear improvement," Schmieder said.
He also said that the group would need to spend over 500 million marks during the 1997 business year for restructuring costs.
"Normally we would spend something around 400 million marks on normal restructuring, but that will not be enough for this year. We expect to spend over 500 million marks this year," Schmieder said.

Hoechst, Europe's largest chemicals group, will on Tuesday ask its shareholders to approve a planned restructuring whereby Hoechst AG would be turned into a strategic management holding group, turning the business units into separate operational entities.
